observations: A used automatic transmission/gearbox assembly lies on bare dirt ground, covered in heavy dust, grime and some surface rust/staining.
Wiring harness connectors dangle loose from the case; one connector (purple, photo 1 and 2) is unplugged and exposed to dirt.
A driveshaft/output yoke stub is visible with rubber boot, consistent with a transfer-case-equipped drivetrain part.
Another similar gearbox/transfer case unit is partly visible at left edge of all three photos, plus unrelated engine parts in the background of photo 0.
A yellow paint dot and a faint stamped number (possibly '39' or similar, photo 2) appear on the bell-housing area, but no full part/VIN plate or legible stamp is readable in any photo.
No workshop test bench, stand, fluid, or any testing rig is shown; the unit sits directly on soil.
No tags, barcodes, or Ford part-number stickers are visible anywhere.
Seller's new message is text only, repeating prior claims verbally; no new photo or video was supplied.

proof_requests: Close-up, well-lit photo of any casting/part number or Ford tag on the case or bellhousing.
Video of the gearbox running on a test stand showing shifting and listening for knock.
Photo of drained transmission fluid showing color/cleanliness.
Photo/document of import paperwork supporting Belgium origin.
Close-up of the unplugged purple connector, showing pins are clean and undamaged.
response.reason: The seller's reply adds no new photographic or documentary evidence, only a verbal reassurance, so all claims remain unverifiable and the item must still be priced at worst case as an untested, unconfirmed-fitment used gearbox pending the listed proofs.
